dutySources.human-review: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(5)(b) — 'SHALL NOT BE ISSUED SOLELY ON THE OUTPUT OF AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM WITHOUT HUMAN REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF THE DENIAL BY A LICENSED CLINICIAN, LICENSED PHYSICIAN, OR OTHER REGULATED PROFESSIONAL'
dutySources.impact-assessment: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(3)(f) — 'THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM'S PERFORMANCE, USE, AND OUTCOMES ARE PERIODICALLY REVIEWED TO MAXIMIZE ACCURACY AND RELIABILITY'
dutySources.registration-filing: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(4) — 'SHALL PROVIDE WRITTEN DISCLOSURES TO THE DIVISION, THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES, OR THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH CARE POLICY AND FINANCING, AS APPLICABLE'

sources.appliesTo: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(2) — 'SUBSECTIONS (3), (4), AND (5) OF THIS SECTION APPLY TO: (a) A CARRIER THAT: (I) USES AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM FOR THE PURPOSE OF UTILIZATION REVIEW'

sources.aiSoleBasis: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(5)(b) — 'A CARRIER'S DENIAL OF COVERAGE BASED IN WHOLE OR IN PART ON MEDICAL NECESSITY SHALL NOT BE ISSUED SOLELY ON THE OUTPUT OF AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM'

flags: adjudicated: no `documentation` duty — § 2(3)(e) requires the system to produce and retain 'DOCUMENTATION, AUDIT LOGS, AND MODEL-GOVERNANCE RECORDS IN ORDER TO DEMONSTRATE COMPLIANCE WITH THIS SECTION' — internal retained compliance records, not the vocabulary's 'published documentation of models/training data'

human-review / sole-basis prohibition applies only to denials of coverage based in whole or in part on medical necessity (§ 2(5)(b)); subsections (3)-(4) apply to all utilization review, so decisionsCovered='all' is slightly lossy

subsection (4) disclosures run to state agencies (division / dept. of human services / HCPF), not to consumers — coded as registration-filing; the insurance-adm consumer 'disclosure' param is left unset

§ 2(3)(a)-(d), (g)-(h) impose substantive operating conditions with no matching duty/param keys: determinations based on the individual's clinical data, no sole reliance on group data, nondiscrimination, fair and equitable application, health-data use limited to 'ITS INTENDED OR STATED PURPOSE', and criteria/guideline compliance with other utilization-review law
§ 2(5)(a) expressly permits AI 'TO ASSIST WITH UTILIZATION REVIEW, INCLUDING EXPEDITED APPROVALS'
behavioral health administrative services organizations and managed care entities (Medicaid/behavioral-health payers) are also bound — quasi-public payers included under a company categorization
no penalty or enforcement provision in the text — exposure omitted (silence is silence)
